📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we've tested 170+ mattresses at Tom's Guide to find the best mattresses of 2026 for all sleepers, body types and budgets. After testing them across all four key areas of a mattress that most affect sleep comfort (see our mattress methodology for more), three mattresses stand head and shoulders above the rest when it comes to performance and sleep comfort for the price in this year's Black Friday mattress sales:.

Best for all sleep styles and for back painThe Saatva Classic is highest scoring mattress we've tested, delivering excellent pressure relief and cooling comfort in every sleep position. However, like the Helix, the Saatva isn't designed to support co-sleepers who weigh over 300lbs each – but the DreamCloud can. The Saatva is presently on sale for the best price we've seen since Labor Day, with a queen costing $1,804 (was $2,229).

It has been revealed that best value for couples and for heavier peopleWhile the DreamCloud lacks the luxury trimmings of the Saatva, it delivers good back support, pressure relief and edge support at a third of the cost. Yes it retained some heat during our cooling test, but not enough to scare off hot sleepers. Right now the DreamCloud is even better value than usual with a queen priced $699 and bundled with $599 of free bedding – it's rare to see free gifts with this.

Best for side sleepers with hip painThere isn't much separating the Helix and Saatva on paper, but from our testing we know that the feel of these luxury hotel-style mattress is different. While Saatva keeps you on top of the bed, Helix lets you sink in for a deep body-hug. That alone makes it the better choice if you have shoulder and hip pain when side sleeping. There's 25% off for Black Friday, with a queen priced $1,874 (was $2,498).

For the latest price cuts, see our Black Friday mattress deals tracked live guide.

We put the Saatva Classic, the DreamCloud Classic Hybrid, and the Helix Midnight Luxe through the same set of standardised lab tests. We also analysed each mattress in terms of value for money. Here's how each mattress stacks up:.

Good pressure relief in a mattress combines two things: cushioning at the touch points, to reduce pressure build-up, and support for your spine to prevent strain or 'hammocking'. In other words, it's the 'aaah' feeling you get when you climb into a mattress that's just right for you. The Saatva, DreamCloud and Helix scored well in this area.

The Saatva earned a 5 out of 5 pressure relief test score for all sleep positions. (We tested the Luxury Firm Saatva Classic but it's available in three feels: Plush Soft, Luxury Firm and Firm). The surface contours lightly to your body, but springs back instantly to deliver constant and responsive pressure relief.

Recent findings suggest that the Helix scored a 4.5 out of 5 score in the same test, with sink-in foams cushioning our shoulders and hips. While it's the best mattress for side sleepers, it didn't score full marks like the Saatva because it wasn't as responsive – the foams took longer to bounce back, and some of our testers found the Helix harder to move around on.

Industry observers note that the DreamCloud Classic scored a 4 out of 5 in our pressure relief test, which is still an excellent score. It's lower than the Saatva and Helix because because contouring isn't quite as effective, and the materials took longer than the Helix to bounce back. There was also less lumbar support, but still impressive for a mid-range bed-in-a-box.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

If you're waking up most nights because you're too hot or too cold, you need a matter with better temperature regulation. The better ones we've tested all use a breathable construction to stop stuffy heat from pooling in the mattress, leading to overheating.

The Saatva Classic scored 5 out of 5 in our temperature regulation test, ranking just underneath our best cooling mattress of the year the Bear Elite Hybrid. With our tester lying on the bed, the Saatva's temperature crept up by just 6.3°F (compared to 7.3°F from the DreamCloud and 9°F on the Helix.) The Bear had a faster heat dissipation rate, shedding over eight degrees of heat in a minute compared to a 3°F shed from the Saatva.

It has been revealed that at 1.12°F the DreamCloud had a faster dissipation rate than the Saatva Classic (1.26°F per minute), but it onboarded more heat: the DreamCloud had a Maximum Temperature Increase of 7.3°F, compared to 6.3°F on the Saatva and 9°F on the Helix. Subjective feedback from our testers was also mixed from the DreamCloud, with three out of five saying it felt warm to sleep on.

Sources indicate that A mattress with good motion isolation can eat up movement from a restless partner, meaning you stand a better chance of sleeping peacefully through the night. But motion isolation is something even the best hybrid mattresses struggle with, as by design the layers of springs and coils add far more bounce to the bed than what you'd get from a memory foam mattress.

In a recent development, we could see this 'bounce' during testing for all three mattresses. The Helix was best at absorbing initial force (just... it's impact rate of 7.4 is below the 7.8 and 7.9 of the Saatva and DreamCloud, respectively), as that thick, soft top eats up force.

But the Saatva Classic has the fastest decay rate at 1.703 — in under two seconds, movement came to a stop.

Sources indicate that strong edge support means you can lie on the side of your mattress without sliding off (a big deal for bed sharers). It also makes getting in and out of bed more comfortable, as you have a sturdy base to push against. We use a 25kg weight to assess the edge support on all mattresses we test.

According to recent reports, the Saatva Classic has the best edge support of any bed we've come across. Foam railings deliver extra support to the sides, meaning our weight hardly sank (it showed 1" less sink at the foot of the bed than in the equivalent position on the Helix or DreamCloud).

Yes, you can sit and lie comfortable on both the DreamCloud Classic and the Helix Midnight Luxe... but you can park a truck on the edge of the Saatva.

According to recent reports, alongside our sleep lab, we test all mattresses at home for at least three weeks. The Saatva Classic, DreamCloud Classic Hybrid and Helix Midnight Luxe have all gone through extensive at-home testing over the past year.

During our Saatva Classic mattress review, our lead tester (and editor) described the Classic as having "the best pressure relief of any mattress we’ve reviewed so far.".

Sources indicate that she noted that you lie on top of the surface while the materials contour to your body, a feel one member of our testing team called "weightless". Add on full-body support and a "gloriously cool-touch surface," and you have one of the best mattresses for back pain you can buy online.

In comparison, our the DreamCloud Classic Hybrid mattress review team found it lacked a little lumbar support. However, our lead tester felt the bed "cushioned" her shoulders while "elevating" her spine, creating full-body comfort when side sleeping.

This had a direct impact on her sleep quality; "I woke less in the night because I wasn’t tossing and turning as much," she explained. Lightweight back sleepers should also feel supported, although heavier members of our team noticed a slight "hamocking" effect.

Made for side sleepers, our Helix Midnight Luxe mattress review team felt it lived up to its promise with "incredible pressure relief to the shoulders and hips.".

In a recent development, it's also highly supportive for back sleepers, which is why our lead tester described it as the only mattress her and her husband have ever agreed on. The plush pillow-top delivers a "hug" that some find stifling — but others described as "cloud-like.".

Industry observers note that right now is the best time to shop from all three brands. Saatva's sale is a step up from the Memorial Day offer, while DreamCloud's free gift sweetens an already excellent value boxed bed. You're unlikely to see a better Saatva mattress sale this year.

According to recent reports, with a Classic Hybrid twin just $349 and a queen $699, the DreamCloud mattress sales are always good value. Sources indicate that following our extensive lab and home testing, we recommend the Saatva Classic mattress to almost everyone. It's breathable, the edge support is impeccable and even the motion isolation is decent. With full-body support and an option for every sleep style, it's our number one pick overall.

In a recent development, but if you're a side sleeper and you want a mattress you sink into, try the Helix Midnight Luxe instead — the cushioning is luxurious and it eases hip and shoulder pain. And while the DreamCloud falls behind in lab results, it earned the title of our favorite mattress in a box because of it's sheer value. If you want a mattress under $1,000 that doesn't skimp on quality, this is the one.

Recent findings suggest that nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Black Friday, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which released in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

It has been revealed that but the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

In a recent development, that stated, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Though it has been supplanted by the Series 12, released earlier this fall, the Series 11 is still a great buy. It lasts up to 24 hours, making it a great option for everyday use and sleep tracking, and a 15-minute charge provides around eight hours of use. It has a strong selection of health features, including wrist temperature sensing, sleep score, ECG, heart-rate monitoring, and hypertension notifications, as well as detailed workout tracking. Compared with the Series 10, this aluminum model’s Ion-X display is twice as scratch-resistant. It’s also water-resistant to 50 meters.

According to recent reports, while it doesn’t have the Series 12’s new processor or updated health-tracking features, the Apple Watch Series 11 is a great pick for your first Apple Watch or as an upgrade from an older model, such as the Series 8. Its large display, durability, and versatile staple features deliver the core Apple Watch experience at a more affordable price, especially if you don’t want Apple’s latest Audio Intelligence features.

Prime Day and Black Friday are the two best times of the year to get the best deals on most purchases. Of course, depending on what you're shopping for, you might find other opportunities throughout the year, but in general, Prime Day and Black Friday have the best sales.

Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Industry observers note that electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then reveals how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

Recent findings suggest that as for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

It has been revealed that back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.

Recent findings suggest that the latest model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

It has been revealed that bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights. Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

Industry observers note that what could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

Sources indicate that prismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac. The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper.

According to recent reports, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail.
  • I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail.
  • In a recent development, it turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail. The reason for this has now become clear, and Apple has done something both fun and clever in macOS 27 to resolve it ….

I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail. Developer Norbert Heger pointed out this is because Apple changed the radius of the corners without changing the grabbable area.

In a recent development, it turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it. The window expects this click to happen in an area of 19 × 19 pixels, located near the window corner. If the window had no rounded corners at all, 62% of that area would lie inside the window. But due to the huge corner radius in Tahoe, most of it – about 75% – now lies outside the window.

At the time, the radius change itself looked like an inexplicable mistake on Apple’s part, and the organization did revert it. However, Macworld’s Michael Simon appears to have discovered the reason for the original change.

The upcoming rounder corners on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR are basically a perfect match for the macOS 26 radii.

According to recent reports, so if you move a window to the corner of the upcoming machine, it would fit perfectly. However, since Apple reverted the corner radius, it would no longer do so. The company solved this by a clever UI transition.

What’s happening there is Golden Gate’s 20-point corner radius is subtly and gradually expanding when It approaches the bottom corner of the screen to match the exact corner of the display, which is much larger. I can’t be certain it’s exactly 26-point, but it sure looks like it to me. The effect is incredible. I’ve watched it like 20 times and I can barely see it changing, yet when it reaches the corner it’s perfectly expanded to match.

Industry observers note that you can see this illustrated by a GIF in the Macworld piece. While the original change annoyed me, Apple’s solution is the perfect example of the company sweating the details.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the recent Microsoft 365 outage was the worst the service had ever experienced, with more than 80% of the company’s servers unresponsive at the worst point. The company has now declared a Code Red to address the way it prevents and responds to major failures in future.

Microsoft has explained more about why it took so long to resolve the glitch and said that it’s urgently working on new approaches to resolve any future incidents in less than an hour ….

Code Red is a common term used to describe the highest priority response to a major problem, pulling a significant number of engineers off their current tasks in order to maximize the resources applied to fixing it.

“Scattered across fragmented internal systems.” 😆.

As someone who works in IT and manages Microsoft products, I thought that was their entire design philosophy.

The senior execs responsible for the service told staff that it was the most customer-impacting incident ever experienced, and has acknowledged that not only was the problem itself unacceptable, but so too was the time taken to resolve it. Reuters got sight of a memo sent to the team.

It was the most ⁠customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson mentioned in a memo to staff on Friday. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo.

One reason it took so long to work out what had happened was because the diagnostic data needed was “scattered across fragmented internal systems.” The memo claims 11 separate Teams chats exchanged more than 11,000 messages as they struggled to work out what exactly had gone wrong.

Industry News: The Cutthroat Business of Shipwrecks

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jstor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in 1627, treasures started to wash up on the beaches of France: diamonds, ebony, precious porcelain, spices, ivory, ambergris, and bezoars.
  • It has been revealed that the disaster promptly threatened to become an international incident.
  • In a recent development, it’s easy to understand why a beachcomber who found a diamond in the sand might want to hold onto it, but there was a legal basis for their claims.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in 1627, treasures started to wash up on the beaches of France: diamonds, ebony, precious porcelain, spices, ivory, ambergris, and bezoars. Two Portuguese ships, so huge they were referred to as “floating cities,” had shipwrecked off the coast of Bordeaux, spilling luxury goods into the waves.

It has been revealed that the disaster promptly threatened to become an international incident. The owners of the cargo (unsurprisingly) wanted their goods back—but the coast dwellers claimed that anything that washed up on shore was theirs by the ancient droit du naufrage, the “right of wreck.”.

In a recent development, it’s easy to understand why a beachcomber who found a diamond in the sand might want to hold onto it, but there was a legal basis for their claims. The “right of wreck” was a long-lived and widespread custom, one that shaped the very architecture of seaside towns: in his travels through Norfolk, Daniel Defoe wrote that the “country people had scarce a barn, or a shed, or a stable…but what was built of old planks, beams, wales and timbers, &c. the wrecks of ships, and ruins of mariners and merchants’ fortunes.”.

According to recent reports, that remarked, in legal terms, the right of wreck was a little more complicated than “finders keepers.” In many places, it wasn’t actually the person who stumbled on the shipwrecked goods who held the right to them; rather, they became the property of the local lord. In the earliest iterations of this idea, poor shipwreck survivors could find themselves roughly stripped of all their goods—as King Richard I of England found when his fleet was unlucky enough to wash up off the coast of Cyprus, circa 1191. His fiancée and his sister were taken as captives by the emperor of the island, who also helped himself to all the treasure they’d been traveling with. (This didn’t end well for the emperor, who lost his throne in the ensuing war.).

Neither wealthy merchants nor traveling kings were particularly enthusiastic about the idea that an accident at sea could mean forfeiting all their cargo. On the other hand, powerful landowners were eager to preserve their right to the occasional random windfall. As international trade increased, the right of wreck was slowly reshaped by centuries of legal wrangling. Courts battling over who could keep what ended up creating, for instance, highly specific legal definitions for terms like “flotsam” (goods that just happened to float to the surface after a wreck) and “jetsam” (goods intentionally tossed from a ship to make it lighter).

Sources indicate that the resulting patchwork of rules meant that every shipwreck was a complex negotiation between competing interests. Usually, the owners of the shipwrecked goods were entitled to their property back, in exchange for some kind of fee. Whether that was a ransom or a fair reward for helping salvage the goods is a matter of perspective.

In a recent development, in 1236, King Henry III of England issued an edict stating that if “man, dog, or cat” escaped the shipwreck alive, finders were obligated to hold on to the wrecked goods for three months, allowing the survivors to claim them in that time. There is a bit of an issue with that rule: it’s easy to see how it could create an incentive for shore dwellers to do away with shipwreck survivors in order to claim their goods (whether those survivors be man, dog, or cat).

According to recent reports, legends of these dark deeds swirled for centuries, but there’s little evidence they really happened. Still, people could be rough in their efforts to “salvage.” In Estonia, for instance, where the local lords were entitled to rewards if they helped to save ships in distress, people developed a habit of launching into enthusiastic “rescue” operations, whether or not there was any real danger.

Get your fix of JSTOR Daily’s best stories in your inbox each Thursday.

In a recent development, A particularly good wreck could spark a feeding frenzy. An account of the wreck of the Golden Grape in 1641 gives a sense of the chaos:.

In a recent development, the first arrivals on the beach contented themselves with staving in barrels and filling linen bags and pockets with raisins or, stripping off their waistcoats, used the sleeves as bags. But soon bands of men appeared from the various villages… Some gangs or men took away a score or two of barrels of raisins or the same number of jars of oil, but they were lucky if they did not have to share their booty with a stronger gang before they could gain a place of safety.

Not everything washes ashore, of course; many of the treasures lost in wrecks sank under the waves. There were fortunes to be made, but in a time before diving equipment, the trouble was how to reach it. In the early modern era, for the most part, even European sailors could hardly swim. But Africans living by the sea in Senegambia and the Gold Coast were highly skilled swimmers and divers—leading them to be targeted by enslavers, who knew their specialized skills could be turned to the recovery of underwater riches. As historian Kevin Dawson writes in “History Below the Waterline: Enslaved Salvage Divers Harvesting Seaports’ Hinter-Seas in the Early Modern Atlantic”:.

Sources indicate that the African-honed expertise that enslaved underwater divers carried throughout the Atlantic world allowed them to quickly recover several tons of gold, silver, and other items from shipwrecks, especially old Spanish treasure hulks. Possessing proficiencies held by few in the world, divers exchanged their unique ability to rapidly produce capital for semi-independent lives of privileged exploitation.

Their skills were so irreplaceable that they were able to negotiate for better treatment than most enslaved people, including a share of what they salvaged. Though, of course, a share isn’t much when you’re doing all the work.

He then shifted focus to the White House and his ballroom, which has yet to be completed. “I want to commiserate with those Reporters and Citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House,” Trump noted. “It hasn’t been properly painted, or taken care of, for years. It has been revealed that “They are mostly gone now, brought back to their point of origin and, hopefully, living a beautiful and idyllic life, and promising, ideally, never to kill innocent people again, but we won’t have to worry about that, because they are GONE but, Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from Faraway Lands,” Trump affirmed. “We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!” Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show ⁠Gérard Depardieu to Face Trial for Allegedly Raping Actress Charlotte ⁠Arnould 50 Years Ago Today: Neil Young Played a 1 A.M. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A upcoming report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either ….

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

It has been revealed that I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Recent findings suggest that some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but right now it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claims that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any intends to make it available outside the firm.

Recent findings suggest that apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In a recent development, in terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand fresh operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman claims Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

Sources indicate that however, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield concerns may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

In a recent development, A Rust library for building communications applications. Signalling, media, codecs, NAT traversal, security, and the conversation model are all Rust crates in this workspace, so a call goes from your code to the wire without a separately installed SIP proxy, media server, or RTP engine. The examples below run on a laptop with nothing installed but Rust; the same crates carry the release-gated interoperability evidence against Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Jambonz, Kamailio, and OpenSIPS. In a recent development, the workspace contains 47 crates. You import one of them; it pulls in everything it needs. The rest are internal layers you never name in your own Cargo.toml.

Deployment backends (Keycloak, LDAP, Redis, Postgres vCon storage, audit and SIEM sinks, SAML, SCIM, WebAuthn, STIR/SHAKEN, IMS AKA) are separate rvoip-* extension crates you add only when you operate that backend. The extension catalog lists them.

Security and transports are configuration, not different APIs: SDES-SRTP in 07-secure-call-srtp, TLS in 08-tls-transport, DTLS-SRTP, G.729, AMR-NB/WB, and Opus behind Cargo features. The full surface is documented in the SIP crate README.

Your SIP or WebRTC caller is bridged to the agent through the Orchestrator; the agent joins as its own AI participant with typed events, control messages, and supervised teardown. Every transport turns into the same objects, so an application written against the conversation model does not care whether a leg arrived over SIP, a browser, or QUIC. That is what lets one Orchestrator bridge them.

Ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. It also summarizes utility records from a major regional ice storm. Finally, it outlines how to choose corridors, plan restoration and keep crews and the public safe around covered conductors.

iOS 27.3 includes many new features for Apple’s built-in apps, but it also introduces design changes on the iPhone across Calendar, Safari, Music, and more. Here’s what’s new.

Apple is always iterating on the design of its software. While major overhauls like iOS 26’s Liquid Glass don’t come along often, the company makes smaller design changes all the time via software updates. In iOS 27.3, which will launch to all users next month, Apple has design changes coming to four popular apps: Health, Calendar, Safari, and Music.

The Health app gets the biggest design changes.

As seen above, Health introduces brand fresh Insights, Longevity, and Browse tabs that replace the previous options and include a variety of fresh UI elements like a top navigation row, personalized prompts and coaching, educational videos, and a lot more.

As the side-by-side above shows, the buttons for search and creating a upcoming event have moved out of the top-right corner and into the bottom of the screen.

Calendar also now shows the year at the top of the screen next to the current month, and has updated the ‘Today’ button to show the current date instead.

Safari introduces an optional new design for tabs: Vertical Tabs. You can enable these inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari for a different approach to tabs across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Here’s an example of vertical tabs on iPhone Duo.

Vertical Tabs won’t be for everyone, but they’ve proven popular in other browsers, so it’s great to see Safari add the option.

According to recent reports, song artwork is now able to break the constraints of a square and blend seamlessly into the scrolling lyrics view. Here are examples from Beta Profiles on X:.

Sources indicate that newly introduced in iOS 27.3 Beta: Animated artwork blends into the Apple Music player in landscape mode, and it looks so good. pic.twitter.com/k8rgSEALGo.

This lyrics view was previously available on iPhone Duo, but now it’s coming to all iPhones.

The 12" SweetNight's design is focused on cooling, with an airflow-enhancing '3D' cover that my fellow testers and I found to be extremely cool-to-the-touch (but more on that later). Its foam is also infused with Phase Change Material (PCM), a specialist cooling fabric found in some of the best cooling mattresses. PCM has been proven to improve human heat dissipation up to 25.6% compared to conventional mattresses.

Recent findings suggest that the 12" EGOHOME does have a graphene-infused cover that the brand calls "cooling", but this is very basic. I found all three beds to be good choices for anyone seeking the best mattress for side sleepers (and I say that as a primary side sleeper), but each did boast different levels of pressure relief.

Sources indicate that in my SweetNight CoolNest mattress review, I found that the CoolNest provided excellent pressure relief for side and back sleeping (both in objective and subjective tests). It has enough give in the shoulder and hip region to relieve the side-sleeper pressure points, but its ultra-quick response time means it's easy to move around on and avoids that "quicksand" feel that some memory foam mattresses have.

According to recent reports, I conducted the EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress review for seven months (the longest I've tested a mattress at home) and found it delivered excellent medium-firm support for all sleep positions. However, another tester (a stomach sleeper) considered it a little too soft for front sleeping, proving that mattress firmness is subjective. That noted, back and side sleepers should feel both comfortable and supported.

As for the CopperFlex Essential, it's clear from our tests that it's strictly for side sleepers. I found it incredibly cushioning when sleeping on it for my Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Essential mattress review, which is surprising as it doesn't have a pillow top. From the moment I unboxed the SweetNight CoolNest, I found it to be incredibly cool to the touch. I even slept on it through summer heatwaves without AC and it still delivered optimal temperature regulation. My experience was backed up by our thermal imaging camera tests, which found that the SweetNight has a rapid cooling rate of 2.1°F per minute (a cooling rate even quicker than the Bear Elite's 1.82°F per minute).

According to recent reports, in contrast, I found that both the CopperFlex Essential and the EGOHOME Black retained heat, especially in the back and shoulder region. Out of the three mattresses, the EGOHOME absorbed the highest amount of heat (15.6°F ), which was definitely noticeable to both me and fellow tester, Ruth Jones. And while the CopperFlex Essential absorbed up to 11.1°F in comparison, its temperature control will pose a problem for hot sleepers.

✅ You want cooler nights: The SweetNight boasts a cool-to-the-touch cover and heat-dissipating PCM which provides a cooler sleep even during hot weather.

Sources indicate that ✅ You sleep on your side or back: Its medium-firm foam is soft enough to soothe side sleepers but supportive enough for back sleepers. Plus, it's responsive enough for you to change position without feeling 'stuck' in the foam.

✅ You want the best value for money: The EGOHOME Black 12" Foam is the cheapest option, with promo codes adding extra discount to already cheap sale prices.

✅ You're a combination sleeper: I found it to be supportive in all sleep positions, and the medium-firm feel is ideal for side and back sleeping.

✅ You want the most cushioning: Its plush pressure relief is ideal for dedicated side sleepers, even if it's not such a great choice for back and stomach sleepers.

✅ You want generous extras: With a lifetime warranty and a trial that lasts a full year, the CopperFlex boasts the best benefits.

Frances Daniels is a PPA-accredited journalist and Sleep Staff Writer at Tom's Guide with an MA in Magazine Journalism from Cardiff University. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh Yorkers woke up this Thanksgiving morning to drizzly, gray skies along with winds that had sidewalks covered in dead, yellow leaves, though the weather throughout the pre-noon hours was hardly the fearsome nor’easter blast that prompted the postponement till Saturday of Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade.

Still, with wind levels of up to 23 mph – and gusts considerably stronger – the postponement appears to have been justified, and the worst of the storm is yet to come.

Recent findings suggest that the impact of the postponement on performances that had been scheduled for today – marching bands, celebrity appearances, the big Broadway medley involving nine different indicates – was still be dealt with as of this morning. Will Coss, Macy’s executive producer of the parade, told the Today show this morning that organizers are “actively working through all the pieces of our parade, but I have to say there’s an overwhelming positive response.” Related Stories News Mayor Zohran Mamdani Claims Famed Balloons Will Soar Again At Rescheduled Macy's Parade: "It's The Only Inflation We Support In Upcoming York City" News Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed To Saturday Due To Severe Weather; NBC Will Rerun 2025 Parade On Thursday.

Coss continued, “Our performers, our talent, our performance groups, our bands, we’re all coming together to try to figure this out, and we’re optimistic that we’re going to have a really successful parade on Saturday morning.” Watch on Deadline.

While Coss didn’t specify which performances are on schedule, Deadline can confirm that the Broadway medley that was planned in lieu of the traditional individual show performances is a go for Saturday. What Macy’s is calling the “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will go on as planned, with performers from The Lost Boys, The Rocky Horror Show, Wicked, Schmigadoon!, Aladdin, The Book of Mormon and Chicago confirmed. (Hamiilton and the 30th-anniversary tribute to Rent have not weighed in yet, but sources say they are expected to participate).

Paddington the Musical is confirmed to participate in the Saturday broadcast as a separate float, as originally intended.

On Instagram today, Sherri Shepherd, presently portraying Genie in Broadway’s Aladdin, wrote, “Winds won’t stop our participation in the Macys 100 Thanksgiving Day Parade, so tune in Saturday at 8:30am on NBC to catch myself and the cast of Aladdin perform!!”.

In a recent development, on the Schmigadoon! IG page, Brad Oscar, dressed and in character as the Mayor, said in a video, “As mayor of Schmigadoon, I have a proclamation: The Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday at 8:30 a.m. on NBC. See you there.”.

The Book of Mormon had a simple message on its IG page about the date switch: “Ready and psyched.”.

In a recent development, as for other non-Broadway performers originally scheduled for Thursday, reports are filtering in piecemeal on whether they’ll make the move to Saturday. The New York Post has reported that Smash Mouth will perform, and Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete are expected as well, as are the Radio City Rockettes. Other announcements should be coming in over the next day or two.

In a recent development, as for the marching bands, again, piecemeal reports. Texas’ Pride of Pearland Marching Band reportedly raised an extra $350,000 in community donations to cover the additional housing and transportation costs to stay until Saturday, while other marching bands were either still scrambling or had made the decision to bow out of the event due to logistics. In the latter group are the Campo Verde High School Marching Band and some members of the Bowling Green State University Marching Band that were participating in a all-star band group.

#142809. Breaking: Ariana Grande’s Best On-Screen Roles

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1153 w)

Breaking: Ariana Grande’s Best On-Screen Roles

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1153 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ariana Grande may be one of the biggest pop stars in the world, but she’s also a true multi-hyphenate, known for her uncanny impressions and acting chops.
  • Now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the latest movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week.
  • Industry observers note that part of what makes Grande’s acting career so much fun to watch is that she never does what anyone is expecting her to do — and she’s not above extreme silliness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ariana Grande may be one of the biggest pop stars in the world, but she’s also a true multi-hyphenate, known for her uncanny impressions and acting chops. Grande can hit a killer vocal run, produce a sleek beat, and steal a scene with terrific comedic timing. (It’s called range.) Her Hollywood career has grown with her pop star status — she started as a Broadway baby, singing her heart out in the musical 13, and eventually became one of Nickelodeon’s most beloved airheads as she played Cat Valentine on Victorious.

Now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the latest movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week. So what better time to look back at the roles that have helped the megastar get to this point? Here are some of her most impressive moments both on the big and small screens.

Industry observers note that part of what makes Grande’s acting career so much fun to watch is that she never does what anyone is expecting her to do — and she’s not above extreme silliness. That makes her Zoolander 2 performance particularly entertaining. It’s extremely brief, but she pops on-screen just in time to have a wild orgy with Hansel (Owen Wilson). The scene marked her first time meeting Ben Stiller, who she reunites with in Focker-In-Law. She looked back at their meet-cute fondly during a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon: “He was directing me in an orgy scene in Zoolander 2 with a hippo and Susan Sarandon,” she shared. “So right off the bat, we had a comfortability.” —Julyssa Lopez.

In a recent development, grande is one of the best parts of Adam McKay’s 2021 satire Don’t Look Up. She plays Riley Bina, a major pop star who is out-of-touch with the world — and the fact that a humanity-ending comet is headed Earth’s way. Once people start believing PhD student Kate Dibiasky (Jennifer Lawrence) and her advisor Dr. Randall Mindy (Leonardo DiCaprio) about their chilling prediction, Bina performs her new song “Just Look Up” with her cheating boyfriend, DJ Chello (Kid Cudi). The scene finds Grande delivering killer one-liners like, “Listen to the goddamn qualified scientists, we really fucked it up this time” while suspended onstage and sporting a ridiculous get-up of white feathers. According to McKay, many of the song’s lyrics were improvised by Grande. —Maya Georgi.

In 2013, Nickelodeon adapted Gordon Korman’s 2008 novel Swindle, shaping it into a made-for-television heist movie revolving around two friends who set out to recover a $1.2 million baseball card. They form an unlikely group with other kids from their school harboring secret skills, and Grande steps in as a cheerleader with an undercover geeky side. The film came during her Sam & Cat days, and teamed her up with co-star Jennette McCurdy, while also letting her go beyond her flaky Cat persona. —J.L.

According to recent reports, when Grande reprises the role of Glinda for the second half of the Wicked tale, she’s planning her wedding to Prince Fiyero, all of Emerald City idolizes her, and everything is as she always wished — or is it? As Glinda reevaluates her life and decides to change paths to help her friend Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo), there are fewer of the rollicking comedy moments that made Grande’s performance in the first film so fun to watch. But with substantial songs like “I Couldn’t Be Happier,” “The Girl in the Bubble,” and the booming duet “For Good,” she makes clear why she was a natural fit for the iconic role. —Kate Storey.

Recent findings suggest that guest-starring on the campy horror-comedy television show Scream Queens as Chanel #2 was Ariana Grande’s first adult role after leaving Nickelodeon’s Sam & Cat to focus on her music. Creator Ryan Murphy remarked in 2015 that initially, Grande “was just going to do one episode, but she loved the process so much that she wanted to do more.” Even though she played a corpse in a few of those episodes, Ari’s comedic skills shine through, especially in a scene where her character’s ghost visits Emma Roberts’ Chanel #1. Grande is hilarious when speaking about her afterlife in hell. Whether her character is that she’s in a bad mood because Adolf Hitler was motorboating her boobs or that Jesus broke into heaven and stole the dinosaurs, she steals every scene. —Alison Weinflash.

Industry observers note that let’s look beyond the fact that Cat Valentine seemingly has a legitimate lobotomy in the middle of the Victorious run. There would not be an Ariana Grande without the exposure, preparation, and genuine war stories that the cast ofVictorious went through. While the will-they-won’t-they nature of Cat’s relationship with Robbie (Matt Bennett) was finally resolved in the apocalyptic music video for “One Last Time,” the most memorable musical moments of the series all involved Grande: from the karaoke bar rendition of “Give it Up” to the “They didn’t say I couldn’t sing” riff on the Victorious iCarly collab “Leave It All to Shine.” As Cat, Grande earned her place in the Hollywood Arts High School hall of fame and started her path toward becoming a household name. —C.T. Jones.

Recent findings suggest that ariana Grande has hosted SNL three times now, and she always makes her appearances memorable by leveraging her exceptional impersonation skills, showcasing her comedy agility, and refusing to shy away from being wildly silly. We’ve seen her play Jennifer Lawrence during a Family Feud recreation and playing a shy intern who saves her radio station with her ability to sound like everyone from Shakira to Celine Dion. But her most beloved contributions might be in an off-key bridesmaid in the famed Domingo skit and giving us a hilarious take on Home Alone. —J.L.

Grande’s character in Focker In Law, Olivia Jones, is a multi-hyphenate not unlike the actress who portrays her. Just swap the gold records for FBI credentials, throw in vegan cooking chops, and you have a future in-law (to grandpa Jack Byrnes, reprised brilliantly by Robert De Niro) hell-bent on entering the “circle of trust” in record time. Grande plays the ultra-competitive Liv with exacting comedic timing, offering the perfect foil for Ben Stiller’s goofball insecurity. —Shirley Halperin.

It takes self-determination, drive, and a lot of pink to make the world’s most coveted role your own. Ariana Grande wasn’t the frontrunner when Universal first announced it would be making a Wicked film. But the Petal singer fought to claim Glinda’s glitter wand. “Oz has been my safe space for as long as I can remember,” she wrote in an open letter to fans before the film’s premiere. It’s hard to imagine a world where the gleeful shrieks of Grande’s “Popular” outro didn’t exist — and her participation in the John M. Chu duology is a career-defining moment, proof the former Nick star is never far from her musical theater roots. —C.T.J.

It has been revealed that amazon is offering early Black Friday discounts on like-fresh versions of its 2024 Kindles, with prices starting at $161.99 for the Paperwhite Signature Edition. These models are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The firm introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon certified to look and work like new.

Industry observers note that the Like-New Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $161.99 from $224.99, almost 30% off. For that price, you're doubling the storage of a standard Paperwhite and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

It has been revealed that the Like-Latest Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $179.99 from $287.99, almost 40% off. And for that price, you're getting twice the storage for a standard Colorsoft, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-Upcoming Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $251.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Tech Report: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Techstackups

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that on 24 November, Google made its eight Workspace MCP servers generally available and published a latest clause in its API terms.
  • Industry observers note that read the Gmail server's tool list and you'll find that it can search your mail, read threads, create a draft and file things under labels.
  • If you've built an email assistant on the Gmail API, or you run a coding agent with a Google Workspace plugin, you have about two months to work out which side of the rule you're on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on 24 November, Google made its eight Workspace MCP servers generally available and published a latest clause in its API terms. From 1 February 2027, any tool that "is or is driven by an AI Agent" must reach Gmail, Drive, Calendar and the rest of Workspace through those servers.

Industry observers note that read the Gmail server's tool list and you'll find that it can search your mail, read threads, create a draft and file things under labels. It can't send a message, reply, forward, or change a draft after creating it. Those tools exist, but Google's quota page notes they "require partner access and aren't generally available".

If you've built an email assistant on the Gmail API, or you run a coding agent with a Google Workspace plugin, you have about two months to work out which side of the rule you're on.

The fresh Workspace AI Tools Addendum to the Google APIs Terms of Service puts it in one sentence:.

The GWS Access Tool must use a Google MCP where the GWS Access Tool is or is driven by an AI Agent, an AI Harness or an AI model or service employing an AI model.

The next sentence forbids disguising an agent to avoid the classification. Breaking either lets Google "restrict or remove the GWS Access Tool's access" or suspend your account.

In a recent development, there's a technical side too. From the same date, agents that call the REST APIs directly are held to Standard-tier quotas, whatever tier the project has paid for. REST keeps working for them, slowly and in breach of the terms.

Apps that don't involve AI carry on as before. A nightly backup job, a CRM sync or a deterministic script on its own OAuth client is, in Google's words, "not affected by this change".

The addendum also adds data rules that matter to anyone building an agent with memory:.

Industry observers note that the 30-day cap is the one product teams will feel. An assistant that builds a long-term index of your inbox to answer questions about last year's contracts has to rebuild it monthly or drop it.

Coverage is uneven. Docs, Slides and Tasks are close to everything the REST API offers. Gmail and Drive are much thinner.

The Gmail gap is the one that breaks real workflows. An agent that drafts a reply, gets feedback from you and revises it before you hit send can't do the revision step. It has to create a second draft and leave the first one behind.

Drive's gap is similar: an agent can create a report but can't move it into the right folder or share it with the team.

It has been revealed that google hasn't mentioned who qualifies for partner access or when the partner-only Gmail tools will reach everyone. The effect is already visible, though. Anthropic's Google Workspace connector for Claude advertises sending, replying and forwarding email, and moving and trashing Drive files. Those are exactly the operations the public servers lack.

According to recent reports, so a large AI vendor's agent can send your email through an approved channel, while an independent developer's agent, using the same OAuth scopes the user granted, can only leave drafts. Once the addendum takes effect, that independent developer also can't fall back to the REST API without breaching the terms.

The definitions are broad. An "AI Harness" or a tool "driven by" an AI model plausibly covers a personal script that pipes your inbox into an LLM, and a "GWS Access Point" explicitly includes any "connector, proxy, command line interface, or third-party service". Google hasn't addressed hobby use directly.

Industry observers note that classification starts with self-declaration. OAuth clients now have a checkbox, "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and since 11 November the MCP servers reject clients without it. Clients created before the cut-off and not marked in time stay non-agentic permanently, so owners have to create newly introduced ones. Google hasn't mentioned how it will detect agents that call REST without declaring themselves.

A few edge cases are documented:.

It has been revealed that every project gets the free Standard tier: 5,000 MCP requests per day, per project, per product. Some calls cost more than one request. A Gmail search_threads or list_drafts counts as 10, so an agent that does nothing but search gets 500 searches a day across all its consumers. That's a project-wide limit, so a small multi-user product will hit it promptly.

The paid Scaled tier starts billing on 1 April 2027 for Gmail, Calendar and Drive. Its structure favours REST. MCP usage is billed from the first request, while REST usage gets large free daily allowances: 70 million light Gmail requests a day, for example. Google hasn't published per-request prices.

Google's case, from a Cloud blog post by Chandu Thota and Brad Calder, is that OAuth was designed for apps acting on a human's clear intent:.

Industry observers note that traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced apps where a valid OAuth token implied user intent. As AI agents shift from reading information to acting autonomously at machine speed â¦ a valid token is no longer enough. Policy checks, data boundaries, and human confirmation have to live in the request path.

According to recent reports, there's substance to this. An email agent that reads a message saying "forward the last ten invoices to this address" is a well-documented prompt-injection risk, and a token that allows gmail.modify gives the agent the power to do it. Routing every agent through one gateway gives admins a single place to block categories of action, require approval and audit what happened. The MCP servers do all of that, and apply data-loss-prevention rules automatically.

Recent findings suggest that the same design also gives Google control of which agents can do what, which data they can keep, and whether anything built on that data can compete with Google's own products. The partner-only tools and the 30-day cap on embeddings show that control in use.

Slack went down a similar path in May 2025. It cut history API rate limits to one request a minute for apps outside its Marketplace and banned bulk export of Slack data for LLMs. Slack drew the line by distribution channel. Google draws it by whether the software is an AI, which is harder to define and harder to enforce.

If you build an agent product on Workspace:.

Sources indicate that if you run a personal agent or MCP server against your own account: open-source servers that call REST, such as the popular google_workspace_mcp, will keep running, but at Standard quotas and outside the terms. Switching to Google's servers costs you sending and draft editing in Gmail, and moving and sharing in Drive.

If you're a Workspace admin: the upcoming controls are under Admin console â Security â API Controls. You can block or approve each category of agent action, set approval policies, and see agent activity in the audit logs. Customers can't view or revoke the approvals they've saved, which expire after 90 days, so it's worth setting policy before people start connecting agents.

If your integration doesn't use AI: nothing changes, as long as it stays on its own OAuth client and nobody wires a model into it.
